Two cases journal as teardown-check~case=fire and ~case=larder (Harness/KingdomTeardownNativeChecks.cs Case class), proving both the zero-salvage boundary and a genuine positive-salvage delta from the same live production rule. Salvage is attributed by STRIKE-RECEIPT (KingdomConstruction.ReceiptProperty captured before the strike, matched via StrikeSalvageReceiptProperty across every zone stockpile), never by own-chest before/after delta -- OrderStrike returns salvage to the first eligible stockpile zone-wide (Growth/KingdomMaterials.13.StrikeRemovalAndSalvage.cs:114-126), not the original payer, which an own-chest delta with two parallel cases would get wrong. Removal is confirmed by reference (a same-ID replacement object refuses, never counts as gone) and by a same-cell finished-building sweep, not by ID-string absence alone. BLOCKER FOUND AND FIXED (Codex root, source review, pre-native): the receipt must be captured AFTER a successful OrderStrike, never before -- OrderStrike mints a NEW strike-route registry row and rebinds the works to it in the same call (Growth/KingdomMaterials.08.StrikeOrdering.cs:257-261 NewJob, Growth/KingdomMaterials.09.StrikeStampAndCancellation.cs:35 Bind), superseding the paid-construction receipt salvage is tagged against (Growth/KingdomMaterials.13.StrikeRemovalAndSalvage.cs:113). Fixed: capture moved after OrderStrike, plus a Require that the new receipt differs from the pre-strike one. Negative regression is an ORDER PIN only (DevTests test ReceiptIsCapturedAfterTheStrikeNeverBeforeAndMustDifferFromThePreStrikeOne), disclosed as not runtime behaviour proof -- no pure predicate exists to value-test this without the game. FURTHER FIX (Codex root): the handoff to the new strike-route registry row is now RESOLVED BY REFERENCE, not merely id-captured -- after a successful OrderStrike, KingdomConstruction.TryFind(StrikeReceiptId, out row) then KingdomTeardownStrikeRowClaims.IsExpectedStrikeRow (Harness/KingdomTeardownStrikeRowClaims.cs, engine-free pure predicate, mirrors the KingdomQuickstartBuildClaims pattern) Requires row.Route==Strike, row.SubjectId/SourceId==the struck works IDIfAssigned, row.OwnerKey==the settlement owner key, row.ZoneId==the struck zone, row.Phase==Working AND row.PhysicalPhase==StrikeWorking (CORRECTED: OrderStrikeDurable does not return true until ResumeStrikeStamp succeeds, Growth/KingdomMaterials.08.StrikeOrdering.cs:274, which stamps PhysicalPhase.StrikeWorking then transitions Phase to Working via FinishProjection, Growth/KingdomMaterials.09.StrikeStampAndCancellation.cs:51,55-56 -- Phase is never left at NewJob's initial Published once OrderStrike has actually returned true), refusing any mismatch by name. Value-tested positive+8 negatives in DevTests/KingdomTeardownStrikeRowClaimsTests.cs (wrong route incl. the exact old-construction-route failure mode, wrong subject, wrong source, wrong owner, wrong zone, pre-stamp Published phase, missing StrikeWorking physical phase, wrong terminal phase) -- this is real behavioural proof of the predicate, not a source pin, though the harness call-site itself is still only source-pinned. DevTests source pin for KingdomBuilt corrected to forbid only the WRITE form (SetIntProperty), never the read the removal-census sweep legitimately performs. CREW ROOFLESS-DEPARTURE GAP (Codex root, disclosed, not fixed): the enrolled synthetic crew has no home plot, so KingdomLodging.Assignments.cs:135-140 records a roof brink for each of them at the first attended lodging pass that finds them unhoused (Growth/KingdomLodging.BrinkAndObservation.cs:31 KingdomBrink.Record); departure fires KingdomLodgingRules.GraceDays (:32) = KingdomBrinkRules.RoofBrinkWindowDays (Core/KingdomBrinkRules.cs:124) = RoofBrinkWindowPasses(2) * CohabitationDaysPerAttendedPass(3) = 6 days = 7200 ticks after that warned tick (Core/KingdomRules.Economy.cs:12 TicksPerDay=1200). With the first lodging pass plausibly landing near tick 1200-2400, estimated departure falls near tick 8400-9600 -- inside this fixtures 10800-tick budget, before the final check. No roof/tent step was added (none exists as a lawful reusable in-tree harness API at 4c7768f) and departure is NOT frozen or synthesized away: Frame.Check() re-Requires the real production crew count (KingdomResidents.OnRollCount) before touching either case and, if the crew has fallen below its required size, refuses by a named outcome, "case=<fire|larder> outcome=crew-departed onRoll=<n> wanted=<CrewSize> tick=<t>", inside the same Fail() envelope every other named refusal in this scenario uses -- a named REFUSED verb, never a silently stalled incomplete case and never a false pass (fixed at 3272cff; the departure itself remains open, only its surfacing changed). KingdomWaterDebit.cs:156 is the shared reservation authority both lanes call into.
combinations.prerequisites: a founded settlement with an in-progress construction commission (Working phase, unfinished) AND a raid contact/attack resolved against the same zone within the same interval
combinations.invariants: conservation of water: sum of all outstanding reservations against the survey never exceeds the real store census; a raid's compensation debit and a construction job's funding debit against the same store never double-reserve the same drams; custody by reference (the construction job's own Water reservation object is never silently reused or mutated by the raid's debit path)

combinations.name: multiple cities + travel + save/load
combinations.coupling: CORRECTED: production has ONE realm KingdomSystem, not one System per city. A second 'city' is a second, non-seat KingdomSettlement row in System.SettlementTopology (Core/KingdomSystem.z08.SettlementTopology.cs:22, NonSeatSettlements()), each carrying its own KingdomCityBook with its own SettlementId (Core/KingdomSystem.z25.IdentityNormalization.cs:167-178, City.SettlementId assigned per-row), and its own claimed zone (Core/KingdomSystem.z08.Settlements.cs:61, TrySeat/FindNonSeatSettlementByZone). Travel's loaded-index scan is per-zone (Harness/KingdomCity.NativeTravelDemand.cs:38). The shared authority is this single System's settlement-topology registry each non-seat row claims a slot in -- no driver currently founds a second settlement row at all (row 12, NONE), so this coupling is untested even at the single-behaviour level.
combinations.prerequisites: two founded settlements in the same save AND at least one travel (away/return) cycle for a resident of one of them, followed by a save/cold-load
combinations.invariants: settlement isolation WITHIN the one System: two non-seat KingdomSettlement rows carry distinct SettlementId/City books and distinct claimed zones; a travel scan against settlement A's zone never reads or credits settlement B's stockpile/roster; save/cold-load reproduces every settlement row's SettlementId/City/ClaimedZones distinctly (no merged or aliased KingdomSettlement row after reload)
combinations.seed_turn_matrix: one fixed seed; single scenario shape (found city A, found city B, travel one resident of A away and back, save, cold-load, re-assert both cities' rosters/stock unchanged) -- not a sweep, a single bounded chain
combinations.expected_failure_rows: a travel scan against settlement A observing or crediting settlement B's objects; a cold-load that merges two KingdomSettlement rows' SettlementId/City books or loses one
combinations.reusable_seams: NONE -- no existing driver adds a second KingdomSettlement row to the realm System, so this chain has no reachable starting seam at all
